title: Introduce granular capacity slicing and staged eviction policy for dedicated fleets
author: Maya Chen
description: Motivation: Dedicated fleets currently apply coarse-grained tenant reservations which leads to either wasted GPU capacity or noisy neighbors when tenant demand is bursty. This PR introduces a "granular capacity slicing" abstraction that partitions a fleet's committed capacity into small, independently metered slices that map to tenant classes and workload shapes, plus a staged eviction policy that degrades slices progressively instead of global hard drops. The design provides: 1) slice-level soft/hard bands (guarantee vs best-effort) and per-slice burst budgets; 2) a staged eviction controller that demotes slices through degradation phases (flood, degrade, preempt) with measured cooldown windows; 3) a contract enforcer that monitors slice throughput against configured SLO curves and issues corrective actions (scaled back bursts, temporary pacing) before eviction; 4) telemetry and alerting: percentile slice_utilization, slice_starvation_duration, staged_eviction_count and eviction_recovery_time. Implementation notes: new package pkg/fleet/sliceallocator implements slice allocation, weighting and dynamic rebalancer; pkg/fleet/eviction implements staged state machine and safe-drain hooks; API surface additions include FleetCapacityProfile CRD fields (slice_size_units, degrade_windows) and a runtime config flag enable_staged_eviction. Rollout plan: feature gated behind runtime flag; shadow-mode (metrics-only) for two weeks on canary fleets; gradual opt-in for high-commitment customers; automatic rollback if p99 latency regression > 12ms or error-rate increase > 0.5%. Tests: unit tests for allocator, integration tests against the autoscaler simulator with synthetic burst traces, and a full e2e in the dedicated-lab. Backwards compatibility: default behavior unchanged unless FleetCapacityProfile fields are present or runtime flag is enabled. Limitations: does not yet handle cross-cluster slice migration; will follow in a follow-up PR with intercluster leaseback. See linked Linear items for migration to Dedicated UI and API docs updates.

release_notes: Add: Fleet capacity slicing and staged eviction controller; Config: FleetCapacityProfile CRD extends with slice_size_units, degrade_windows, max_rebalance_window; Observability: new metrics slice_utilization_p50/p95/p99, slice_starvation_duration_ms, staged_eviction_count. Rollout: feature gated; shadow mode available. Impact: optional opt-in; no breaking changes by default.
perf_summary: Lab perf: synthetic burst tests show ~6% throughput improvement for high-variance tenants and 8% lower median token cost due to better packing into slices. Worst-case p99 latency increased by 9ms during an aggressive staged-eviction experiment; mitigations (jitter + non-blocking cache drop) reduced p99 regression to 2ms in re-run.
rollback_plan: Disable runtime flag enable_staged_eviction and let slices settle; automated rollback script resets FleetCapacityProfile fields applied during rollout and reverts the canary groups; alerting playbook triggers if p99 latency > 12ms or error-rate delta > 0.5%.
